claim: The previously selected o_proj plus gate/up group-8 INT4 QDQ candidate passed the configured teacher-forced quality-proxy gates on a deterministic held-out WikiText-2 test subset.

candidate.selection_provenance: Selected as the highest-storage-reduction passing mask in the prior 15-mask group-8 search on the hand-authored agent-style corpus; this WikiText subset was not used for candidate selection.

corpus.benchmark_note: WikiText-2 is a standard language-modeling source, but this deterministic 32-window subset and the configured multi-metric gates are not the canonical full WikiText-2 benchmark protocol.

estimated_storage.note: Packed storage is an arithmetic deployment estimate. The measured QDQ quality run retained float32 weights and did not materialize a packed kernel representation.

limitations: Teacher-forced NLL, perplexity, logits, and token agreement are language-modeling proxies, not task accuracy or end-to-end agent success.
The custom 512-token subset is larger than the 155-token selection corpus but remains too small for a production quality claim.
No packed INT4 kernel, runtime compression, throughput, latency, energy, serving cost, or dollars-per-token improvement was measured.
The result applies to the local Qwen3-0.6B checkpoint and does not establish transfer to a larger model.
conclusion: The selective o_proj plus gate/up candidate replicated its pass on independently sourced held-out text: all five configured proxy gates passed over 512 target tokens, while the logical packed-weight estimate remains a 24.629% reduction. This strengthens the model-specific selectivity hypothesis, but it does not yet show lower inference cost because the run used uncompressed float32 QDQ rather than a packed kernel.
